chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie from Mansur ibn Yunus from Is'haq ibn Ammar from Abdul Malik ibn Amr who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is permissible for the owner of the menstruating woman from her?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Everything except the front part in particular.'

key_terms.الْقُبُل: The front part (specifically the vagina in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is permissible for a husband to do with his wife during her menstruation according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling on intimacy during menstruation by stating that everything is permissible except the *qubul* (frontal vaginal canal), thereby distinguishing between general sexual contact and specific intercourse. This view is central to Shia jurisprudence, where scholars debate whether *qubul* refers strictly to the vaginal opening or includes the entire anterior region, often linking it to the Quranic command to 'come from where they come from' (2:222). The narration underscores the permissibility of other forms of closeness, reflecting a nuanced approach to marital relations during the state of *hayd*.
